title: Coconut Hot Chocolate with Soft Meringue
changes_from_base: Made with a can of coconut milk and cocoa instead of milk and cream, and topped with a soft meringue of pasteurised egg white.
summary: A rich, silky hot chocolate made with a whole can of coconut milk, cocoa and dark chocolate, crowned with a soft, glossy meringue.
equipment: electric hand whisk and a clean bowl

ingredients.item: full-fat coconut milk (1 can), well shaken
fine sea salt or table salt
pasteurised egg white (from a carton, about 1 egg white)

steps.title: Cocoa paste
steps.text: Put the cocoa in the saucepan and whisk in the boiling water a little at a time to a smooth paste. Hot water blooms the cocoa and stops lumps forming.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add the coconut milk, brown sugar and salt and heat gently for about 3 minutes, stirring, until the sugar dissolves and the mixture is steaming.

steps.title: Chocolate
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat, whisk in the chopped chocolate until glossy, then add the vanilla. Keep it warm on the lowest heat.

steps.title: Meringue
steps.text: In a clean bowl, whisk the egg white until foamy, then add the sugar a spoonful at a time and whisk for 4-5 minutes more, until it forms soft, shiny peaks.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pour the hot chocolate into three small mugs and spoon a cloud of meringue on top of each.

tips: Any trace of grease or yolk in the bowl stops egg white whipping, so make sure it is spotless.
Add the sugar slowly; tipping it in all at once gives a runny meringue.
Light coconut milk makes a thinner drink; use full-fat for body.
storage: Best served at once. The hot chocolate (without meringue) keeps 2 days in the fridge; reheat gently, whisking, until steaming. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
